member.name: T:GHIElectronics.TinyCLR.EthernetIP.Adapter.AdapterController
member.summary: Runs the device as an EtherNet/IP Adapter (the server side of EIP — what a PLC scanner connects to). Wraps the native OpENer stack with a managed-C# API.

remarks.para: Singleton: only one instance can exist at a time. Disposing or calling resets the singleton flag so a fresh controller can be constructed.

Identity, Message Router, Connection Manager, Assembly, and QoS classes are auto-initialized in if user code didn't already register them. So a minimal adapter that only adds Assembly objects works out-of-the-box.

member.summary: Construct the adapter. Identity values are set on the underlying CIP Identity object but the network stack isn't started yet — call after wiring up assemblies and connection points.
member.param: Human-readable product name (Identity attr 7). Must match the ProdName field in your EDS file.
ODVA-assigned vendor ID (CIP UINT). Must match the VendCode field in your EDS file. ODVA values 1–99 are reserved for specific companies.
CIP device type per Vol 1 Appendix A (e.g. 0x000C = Generic Device).
32-bit serial number (Identity attr 6). Should be unique per physical device — typically read from non-volatile storage.
member.exception: Thrown if another AdapterController is already constructed and hasn't been disposed (singleton enforcement).

member.name: E:GHIElectronics.TinyCLR.EthernetIP.Adapter.AdapterController.ForwardOpenDetected
member.summary:
Fires when a Forward Open (regular or large) succeeds — a CIP connection is now open. large argument is true for Large Forward Open (service 0x5B), false for regular (service 0x54).
As of Phase 3.5 this only fires on successful Forward Opens; failed attempts (resource exhaustion, electronic key mismatch, etc.) no longer trigger a phantom event.

member.name: M:GHIElectronics.TinyCLR.EthernetIP.Adapter.AdapterController.Enable
member.summary: Start the EtherNet/IP stack: opens the four CIP sockets (TCP 44818, UDP 44818 unicast + broadcast, UDP 2222 for Class 1), spawns the OpENer processing thread, and auto-creates any standard CIP class (Identity, Message Router, Connection Manager, Assembly, QoS) that user code didn't already register via AddCipClass.
member.remarks: Idempotent guard: throws if already enabled. Use (or ) to tear down before re-enabling.
member.exception: Thrown if the controller is already enabled.

member.name: M:GHIElectronics.TinyCLR.EthernetIP.Adapter.AdapterController.Disable
member.summary: Stop the EtherNet/IP stack. Equivalent to . Idempotent — safe to call multiple times. Resets the singleton flag so a fresh controller can be constructed afterwards.

member.name: M:GHIElectronics.TinyCLR.EthernetIP.Adapter.AdapterController.Dispose
member.summary: Tear down all native state cleanly: signals g_end_stack=1, polls up to 1 s for the OpENer thread to terminate (during which it calls ShutdownCipStack to close all CIP connections and delete every registered class), frees the 8 KB thread stack, and resets the singleton flags so a fresh can be constructed. Idempotent. Suitable for use in a using block.

member.name: M:GHIElectronics.TinyCLR.EthernetIP.Adapter.AdapterController.EnableHeaderO2T(System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Toggle the 32-bit Run/Idle header on O→T (output) Class-1 data. Must be true when talking to Allen-Bradley ControlLogix/CompactLogix scanners — they always prepend a Run/Idle header. False for most other scanner brands (HMS Anybus, Codesys). Default: false.
Symptom of wrong setting: the first 4 bytes of your output assembly oscillate between 0x00000000 and 0x00000001 every cycle instead of holding real scanner-written data.

member.name: M:GHIElectronics.TinyCLR.EthernetIP.Adapter.AdapterController.EnableHeaderT2O(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Toggle the 32-bit Run/Idle header on T→O (input) Class-1 data. Less commonly required than O2T; defaults to false. Enable if your scanner's configuration expects it.
